massachusetts.rufada_status: Massachusetts has NOT adopted RUFADAA. No digital-assets act exists in the Massachusetts General Laws, and the probate code (M.G.L. c. 190B) has no digital-assets article. Bills to adopt it (H.4639 and S.1110 in the 194th General Court) were reported favorably in 2025-2026 but have not been enacted. Massachusetts is one of only three states that have not adopted RUFADAA.
massachusetts.custodian_access: There is no Massachusetts statute forcing a custodian to disclose an account to a fiduciary. A personal representative's authority comes only from the general probate duty to take possession of the decedent's property (M.G.L. c. 190B, section 3-709) and to inventory it (section 3-706), which runs to the property, not to the provider. In practice the custodian decides under its own terms of service, and the federal Stored Communications Act generally bars a provider from disclosing the contents of emails and messages without the user's consent or a court order. There is no statutory 60-day deadline for a custodian to respond.
massachusetts.user_direction: Because there is no state statute, the user's own planning does all the work: set up each platform's online tool (Google Inactive Account Manager, Apple Legacy Contact, Meta legacy contact), and put express digital-asset authority in the will, trust, or durable power of attorney, naming who may access which accounts. Without a statute there is no legally fixed priority order, so the platform's tool and the written documents should agree with each other.
massachusetts.terms_of_service: Yes — in Massachusetts the custodian's terms of service effectively control, since no state law overrides them. If the user left no direction, the family must ask the custodian under its deceased-user process, and the custodian may refuse, delete, or memorialize the account as its terms allow. A probate court order can sometimes compel access, but there is no statute guaranteeing it.
massachusetts.platform_tools: Google Inactive Account Manager lets the user name a trusted contact who gets access or deletion after a set period of inactivity; Apple Legacy Contact lets a designated person request access with an access key and death certificate; Meta (Facebook and Instagram) offers a legacy contact or memorialization, and requires a death certificate and proof of authority for removal or access. Each platform has its own request form and proof requirements.
massachusetts.what_to_do: 1. Inventory every account, device, password manager, and crypto wallet, including any seed phrases stored at home. 2. Check whether the person set up Google Inactive Account Manager, an Apple Legacy Contact, or a Meta legacy contact. 3. Gather the will, trust, or power of attorney and the letters of appointment from the Probate and Family Court. 4. Contact each custodian with a death certificate and proof of authority and follow its deceased-user process. 5. If a custodian refuses access to message content, ask a probate attorney about a court order, since there is no statute to rely on.
massachusetts.state_statute: No RUFADAA statute. General probate authority only: M.G.L. c. 190B, sections 3-706 and 3-709.
massachusetts.agency_name: Massachusetts Attorney General, Consumer Advocacy and Response Division
massachusetts.state_note: Massachusetts is one of only three states that still has no RUFADAA law at all, so families here depend entirely on platform tools and careful estate documents.

michigan.rufada_status: Michigan adopted its version of the act in 2016 as the Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act, Act 59 of 2016, effective June 27, 2016, codified at MCL sections 700.1001 and following.
michigan.custodian_access: A fiduciary (personal representative, conservator, agent, or trustee) can get a catalogue of electronic communications — who the user communicated with, when, and at what address — and other digital assets such as photos, files, and online accounts. The content of emails and messages is disclosed only if the user consented or a court orders it. The custodian may grant full access, partial access, or a copy of the assets, and may demand a written request, a death certificate, proof of fiduciary authority, and the account identifier. The custodian must comply within 60 days of receiving the required documents, and a fiduciary who is refused can ask the court for an order compelling disclosure.
michigan.user_direction: The user can direct disclosure through the custodian's online tool, or in a will, trust, power of attorney, or other written record. Under Michigan's act, a direction made through an online tool that can be changed or deleted at any time overrides a contrary direction in a will, trust, or power of attorney. If no online tool was used, the will, trust, or power of attorney controls, and either user direction overrides a contrary term in the custodian's terms of service.
michigan.terms_of_service: The terms of service cannot override the user's direction given through an online tool or in a will, trust, or power of attorney. If the user left no direction at all, the terms of service may modify or eliminate the fiduciary's access, and the act's default rules apply — the fiduciary gets the catalogue and other digital assets, but not message content without consent or a court order.
michigan.platform_tools: Google Inactive Account Manager lets the user name a trusted contact who gets access or deletion after a set period of inactivity; Apple Legacy Contact lets a designated person request access with an access key and death certificate; Meta (Facebook and Instagram) offers a legacy contact or memorialization, and requires a death certificate and proof of authority for removal or access. Each platform has its own request form and proof requirements.
michigan.what_to_do: 1. Inventory every account, device, password manager, and crypto wallet. 2. Check whether the person set up Google Inactive Account Manager, an Apple Legacy Contact, or a Meta legacy contact. 3. Gather the will, trust, or power of attorney and the letters of authority from the probate court. 4. Send each custodian a written request with a death certificate, proof of authority, and the account identifier. 5. If the custodian refuses or 60 days pass, ask the probate court for an order compelling disclosure.
michigan.state_statute: MCL sections 700.1001 to 700.1017 (Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act, 2016 PA 59).
michigan.agency_name: Michigan Department of Attorney General, Consumer Protection Team
michigan.state_note: Michigan's act was shaped with input from the State Bar's Elder Law and Probate sections, and it expressly treats a guardian, special fiduciary, and parent of a minor child as conservators for digital-asset purposes.
sources: Michigan Legislature, MCL Chapter 700, Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (Act 59 of 2016) — https://legislature.mi.gov/documents/mcl/archive/2021/September/mcl-Act-59-of-2016.pdf

new jersey.rufada_status: New Jersey adopted the Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act in 2017 (Assembly Bill 3433, P.L. 2017, c. 237), approved September 13, 2017 and effective 90 days later, codified at N.J.S.A. sections 3B:14-61.1 to 3B:14-61.18.
new jersey.custodian_access: A fiduciary (executor, administrator, guardian, agent, or trustee) can get a catalogue of electronic communications — who the user communicated with, when, and at what address — and other digital assets such as photos, files, and online accounts. The content of emails and messages is disclosed only if the user consented or a court orders it. The custodian may grant full access, partial access, or a copy of the assets, and may demand a written request, a death certificate, proof of fiduciary authority, and the account identifier. The custodian must comply within 60 days of receiving the required documents, and a fiduciary who is refused can ask the court for an order compelling disclosure.
new jersey.user_direction: The user can direct disclosure through the custodian's online tool, or in a will, trust, power of attorney, or other written record. The priority order is fixed by statute: a direction made through an online tool overrides a contrary direction in a will, trust, or power of attorney; if no online tool was used, the will, trust, or power of attorney controls; and either user direction overrides a contrary term in the custodian's terms of service.
new jersey.terms_of_service: The terms of service cannot override the user's direction given through an online tool or in a will, trust, or power of attorney. If the user left no direction at all, the terms of service govern first, and if they say nothing about fiduciary access, the act's default rules apply — the fiduciary gets the catalogue and other digital assets, but not message content without consent or a court order.
new jersey.platform_tools: Google Inactive Account Manager lets the user name a trusted contact who gets access or deletion after a set period of inactivity; Apple Legacy Contact lets a designated person request access with an access key and death certificate; Meta (Facebook and Instagram) offers a legacy contact or memorialization, and requires a death certificate and proof of authority for removal or access. Each platform has its own request form and proof requirements.
new jersey.what_to_do: 1. Inventory every account, device, password manager, and crypto wallet. 2. Check whether the person set up Google Inactive Account Manager, an Apple Legacy Contact, or a Meta legacy contact. 3. Gather the will, trust, or power of attorney and the letters testamentary or letters of administration from the Surrogate's Court. 4. Send each custodian a written request with a death certificate, proof of authority, and the account identifier. 5. If the custodian refuses or 60 days pass, ask the Superior Court for an order compelling disclosure.
new jersey.state_statute: N.J.S.A. sections 3B:14-61.1 to 3B:14-61.18 (Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act, P.L. 2017, c. 237).
new jersey.agency_name: New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs
new jersey.state_note: New Jersey's act passed both houses unanimously in 2017, and it expressly covers guardians of incapacitated persons — a court can grant a guardian access to digital assets after a hearing.
